market_context: U.S. futures were near flat to modestly higher before the open, with S&P 500 futures up about 0.1% and Nasdaq 100 futures roughly unchanged. Elevated Treasury yields near 5.25%-5.30% and high oil prices remain headwinds, while ADP employment, GDP, core PCE inflation, and EIA oil-inventory data are scheduled catalysts; early market reporting later showed stocks trading higher, with Nasdaq outperforming.

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were modestly positive before the open, and later reporting indicated the S&P 500 was up about 0.5% during the session. That momentum should support a small gain by the close, although the 5.28% 10-year yield and inflation data create downside risk.

Nasdaq 100 futures were approximately flat to slightly higher premarket, while later reporting showed the Nasdaq composite outperforming with a gain near 0.9%. Technology may continue to lead if yields stabilize, though the high-rate environment limits confidence.

Semiconductors were a focal point ahead of Micron earnings, and premarket coverage described futures as stable while investors focused on chip-sector results. A modest risk-on bid could lift NVDA, but no company-specific catalyst identified in the available information makes this a low-confidence call.

Tesla is particularly sensitive to long-term borrowing costs, and the 10-year Treasury yield remains near multi-year highs around 5.28%. With futures only modestly positive and no specific Tesla catalyst found, valuation pressure could produce a small underperformance.
